MSI-deployed add-ins require the file:/// prefix on the Manifest registry value; without it the VSTO runtime cannot resolve the deployment manifest. An MSI built from the template as written would not load.

Signed the deployment manifest first; the deployment manifest embeds a hash of the application manifest, so that order is invalidated by the later app-manifest signature. Corrected to -Update app manifest, then -Update .vsto with -AppManifest.

The ClickOnce registry example carried |vstolocal, which opts OUT of the ClickOnce cache and belongs to Windows Installer deployments — it contradicted the install/update model the same section described.

'Changing the publish URL breaks all installed clients; treat as permanent' overstates: it is recoverable via setup.exe /url=. The real constraint is the deploymentProvider codebase. Advice kept, framing fixed.
Computer-assigned packages install at computer STARTUP; user-assigned install at logon. The step described a computer-configuration package installing at next login.
The documented restriction is version-scoped (same version, different installation technologies). Different-version coexistence is supported, subject to bitness.

id.symbol: VSTO logging via EnableLogging registry value

rationale: No documented EnableLogging value under HKCU\Software\Microsoft\VSTO\Security. Startup logging is enabled with the VSTO_LOGALERTS environment variable; the log is <add-in>.vsto.log beside the deployment manifest. VSTOInstaller.log is a different tool's artifact.
A VSTO add-in is a class library in the Office host process; a component cannot select the CLR — only an application's own config can. Reframed as a targeting/prerequisite issue.
Office LTSC 2021 has NO Extended Support phase — five years of Mainstream Support ending 2026-10-13. Relabeled 'end of support'.
Receives cumulative security AND reliability/quality updates with no announced end of support; 'maintenance mode, security fixes only' overstates the freeze.

FRESHNESS FAILURE, not an authoring error: true when written, but from Version 2606 (July 2026) SAEC receives Monthly Enterprise builds and 'Monthly Channel' is no longer a channel name. Staging lever is now version pinning/rollback. Carries a check-current-policy caveat.

Framing was backwards. Learn attributes the access-violation hazard to ReleaseComObject and explicitly suggests FinalReleaseComObject when deterministic release is wanted. Reviewable defect is releasing an RCW others may hold (singletons, caller-supplied objects) — including the skill's own ItemAdd 'FIX'.
Value2 is typed object; the only difference from Value is that it never uses Currency or Date (dates arrive as OADate double). It still returns string/bool/error values.

id.symbol: background-thread OM call is an STA violation

rationale: Calls are automatically marshaled across the STA boundary; the documented failure is a rejected call surfacing as COMException (application busy / RPC_E_SERVERCALL_RETRYLATER) plus blocking. Rule restated as 'needs COMException handling with retry, or marshal to UI thread'.

ThisAddIn_Shutdown is not raised when Outlook exits (only when the user disables the add-in), so unsubscribe code there silently never runs. Outlook cleanup belongs on Application.Quit or Explorer.Close. Fixed in VSTO-development and VSTO-review.

Any CPU (the Office project default) runs under both 32-bit and 64-bit Office; bitness only matters when deliberately targeting x86/x64 for native interop. Learn says you typically should not change the setting.

Listed as a common upgrade breakage, but parsing got MORE lenient in that window — 3.11 widened fromisoformat to most ISO 8601 including the Z suffix, and 3.12 documents no stricter-parsing change. SAME CLASS AS THE VSTO-REVIEW REVERSALS: the review skill's example of the bug was actually the documented FIX. `lambda i: i` shadows the loop variable via its parameter and does not capture it; binding-by-default-argument is what Python's FAQ prescribes as the cure. A reviewer following this would flag correct code and miss the real parameterless capture. Verified empirically.

Only the CLI use is deprecated — packaging.python.org states setup.py as a setuptools CONFIG file 'is absolutely fine'. Scoped to invoking python setup.py <command>, with pyproject.toml still preferred for new metadata.

Formula is correct but the i.i.d./serially-uncorrelated assumption was implicit — and sat in tension with the same skill's fat-tails-and-clustering warning. Assumption now stated in backtesting-validation and quant-code-review. An internal inconsistency the gate surfaced, not a factual error.

'annual return / max drawdown' matches modern general usage, but Young's canonical 1991 definition pins a trailing 36-month window and a compound (CAGR) numerator. Labeled as the general form with the window/return convention called out.

Preferring linalg.solve to an explicit inverse is settled numerical-analysis practice but appears nowhere in the NumPy/SciPy docs, which warn only about singular/ill-conditioned input. Kept as a review item, labeled craft rather than citable rule.

Sat in the skill's most load-bearing section (the look-ahead hunt) and was wrong: pandas ewm has NO center parameter and its weights run strictly backward from t, so it cannot use future points. Verified empirically — perturbing the last observation left every earlier ewm mean bit-identical. Split from the (correct) centered-rolling claim and replaced with ewm's real hazards: forgetting to shift(1) the feature, and fitting span/halflife on the full sample.

Close enough to mislead, far enough to matter for a published risk number: pandas demeans by the EW mean with bias=False, RiskMetrics uses the raw second moment about zero with adjust=False at lambda=0.94 (measured ~0.01042 vs ~0.01050). Relabeled EWMA-style with the exact adjustment to get RiskMetrics.

Hash-checking mode requires EVERY requirement including transitive ones pinned with == and hashed, so it only works against a fully-compiled lockfile. The skill implied it but never said it; a partially-pinned file fails the install outright.

COVERAGE RECORD: the print-geometry core verified by computation rather than citation — US Letter tri-fold 3.6875+3.6875+3.625=11.000in exactly (tuck panel 1.59mm narrower, inside the 1/16-1/8in trade range); A4 gate-fold 74.25+148.5+74.25=297.0mm; Z-fold 297/3=99.0mm equal panels; saddle-stitch pages=4x sheets; spine pairing sums to n+1 for n=8,12,16. Bleed 3mm/0.125in is a trade convention with no standards-body spec (and the two figures are parallel conventions, not an exact conversion: 3mm=0.1181in).

The first draft probed support via `Application.WorksheetFunction.Parent.Range("A1").Formula2` — nonsense (WorksheetFunction.Parent is Application; Application.Range needs an active sheet) and, worse, early-bound: a project that names `.Formula2` anywhere fails to COMPILE on an Excel whose type library predates it, so the fallback can never run. Replaced with an Object-typed late-bound probe AND a late-bound write. This is the 'verification step that cannot verify' class again — a feature-detect that the compiler kills before it executes.

Drafted `Provider=MSOLEDBSQL;...Integrated Security=SSPI;`. Microsoft states ADO applications using the OLE DB Driver for SQL Server must supply BOTH `Provider=MSOLEDBSQL19` (or MSOLEDBSQL) AND `DataTypeCompatibility=80`. Omitting the latter is the classic works-in-the-UDL-tester/fails-in-VBA. Also added that `Use Encryption for Data` defaults to Mandatory on the v19 driver, which refuses servers without a trusted certificate.

The bulk-append recipe called `lo.Resize` while stating only that the range must include headers. The reference adds two more preconditions: the header must stay in the SAME row, the new range must OVERLAP the original, and the result must contain a header row AND at least one row of data — so a table cannot be resized down to zero data rows. Also 'no cells are inserted or moved', i.e. content below the table is overwritten rather than pushed down.

Verified before shipping rather than after: MS explicitly recommends passing SourceData as a STRING naming workbook/worksheet/range or a defined name, because 'passing a Range object may cause type mismatch errors unexpectedly'. Also confirmed xlPivotTableVersionCurrent is disallowed and raises, and that omitting Version yields xlPivotTableVersion12. All three are in the skill as written.
